column1: # nv-rs's own options in the run's Fallout.ini (crates/host/src/game_ini.rs; measure/ini/DESIGN.md).
# One row per key: section, key, the environment variable that wins over it (tests and scripts
# only), the value the generated file writes, and the one comment line written above the key.
# That value is the built-in default of a play run (crates/host/src/fixes.rs; a test holds the
# two together), and Play.exe and the generated file take it from here: they have none of their own.
# scripts/game-ini-sections.sh writes distribution/nv-rs-sections.ini from this table; the
# [nv-rs Fixes] rows are written commented out, so sPreset decides until a line is uncommented.

column5: fixes = nv-rs's fixes on (recommended); vanilla = exactly the original game's behaviour.
1 = the game's window has no frame and fills the screen (the default); 0 = the window as the game makes it.
vulkan = the game drawn on Vulkan (the default; Direct3D 12 on a graphics card without Vulkan); d3d9 = drawn by Direct3D 9, as the original draws it (the fallback).
Most frames a second in play, with the fixes' uncapped frame rate; 0 = no limit.
Most frames a second in menus (main menu, Pip-Boy, dialogue, inventory, pause); 0 = no limit of their own.
1 = the frame rate shown in the top-right corner from the start; 0 = hidden until F11 (the default). F11 in the game shows or hides it (Vulkan only).
1 = the game's threads take turns, one at a time (the fallback); 0 = side by side on their own cores.
1 = the Direct3D 9 calls go to a drawing thread of their own; 0 = on the game's threads, as the original makes them.
Uncapped frame rate: the game's frame step without its sleep, so frames are not held to the original's pace (iFrameLimit paces it).
High-frame-rate landing: the player landing standing still falls as far as at 60 frames a second.
High-frame-rate slow motion: the game's time multiplier moves to its target by the time passed, not by the frame.
Menu frame limit: menus at most iMenuFrameLimit frames a second, loading screens unlimited (only with bUncap).
Dragged bodies by time: a held body's pull is scaled by the frame's time, as at 60 frames a second.
Smooth physics drawing: dropped and thrown items, ragdolls and debris are drawn between the physics steps, not frozen on frames without one.
Mod fit worn question: fitting a weapon mod asks whether the mod is worn before removing it, not after.
Dialogue topic index: the topic that holds a dialogue line is looked up, not searched for (the same answers, faster loads with dialogue mods).
Shaders compiled ahead of first use: the graphics driver compiles each of the game's shaders in the menus, not at its first use in play.
IO wait ends on completion: the wait for queued loads (a cell border, a load, a save) ends when they are done, not at its next 50 ms step.
Half-loaded actor's level change: an actor moved to another AI level while its saved data loads (running fast across cells) no longer crashes the game.
Thread races: a new thread's scrap heap, the debug texts and console prints, the face-gen lock's count and the editor-marker pass of a loaded model are safe when the game's threads meet.
Texture files read before the renderer's lock: a texture file is read and unpacked before the renderer's lock is taken, so drawing does not wait for it.
Cell entry waits for its own cell: crossing into a new outdoor cell no longer pauses for the row of cells loaded ahead; they load in the background, after what the cell entered needs.

Cell offsets for every plugin: a cell of a plugin, or of a master without its cell offsets (YUP, TTW), is found by a table built from the plugin at load instead of a search of the file each time a cell loads (the same cells are found).
V.A.T.S. waits only for the camera: a target's hit chances show as soon as the camera reaches it, not after a fixed 2 seconds.
Causes keep no witness lists: projectiles and explosions no longer copy their actor's detection list, which every save wrote out (save bloat).
Radio song lengths: a radio song never takes the length of the song before it on its channel, and a song with no length no longer hangs the music thread.
Facial hair by race folder: facial hair made for one race's head is offered only to that race in the character menu.
No distant water under the Strip: The Strip gets "No LOD Water" as it loads, so the distant water under its ground, never seen, is never made.

Direct file access: the game's files are opened, read and written by the thread that asks, without the file thread, the limit of 512 open files (about 140 plugins) or the 2 GB limit on a file or an archive.
Co-save keeps other plugins: a co-save's parts from plugins not built in (JohnnyGuitar's, ShowOff's and the others not built in yet) are written back while the same files are loaded.
JIP co-save fixes (JohnnyGuitar NVSE's): JIP LN NVSE's extra data is saved with the right sizes, as VNV's co-saves have it, and JIP's own damaged version is not read.
JIP vanilla commands: JIP LN NVSE's versions of seven of the game's commands (MenuMode, GetItemCount, IsInList, HasPerk for followers and others), once JIP is built in.
Script error loop guard: an error inside a script's error handler is not sent to the handlers again.
Image-space event form check: OnRemoveIMOD only for an image-space modifier form's instance that ran out, not for depth of field or blur.

Script reference checks (the key keeps its old name): a reference handed to a script with parts missing no longer stops the game: an inventory reference with no base form or cell, or a door whose teleport or lock data or linked door is missing, answers 0 in the door, key and cell owner commands (GetLinkedDoor, GetDoorTeleportX..Rot, SetDoorTeleport, SetOpenKey, GetParentCellOwner, GetParentCellOwningFactionRequiredRank); and the inventory references' own slips: a removed stack leaves the container's entry before its data is freed, a sale ends with its event, a container entry without a form is passed over; HasOwnership and IsOwned on a reference with no cell or base form answer 0, the cell scans pass over a reference with no base form, and GetNextRef on a scan that ended in the console or was never built answers as its first call did (the error, 0); GetDoorSound on a door without that sound answers 0 (and on no form prints nothing in the console), GetLevCreatureRefs and GetLevCharacterRefs pass over a leveled entry without a form, GenericCheckForm passes over an empty node of the list, and IsRefInList finds nothing in a reference's missing base form.
Script array and string size caps: arrays stop at 8,388,608 elements and repeated empty text at 64 MiB; a bad format string no longer ends the game.
Script missing array guard: ar_Count and ar_GetNth on a missing array answer 0, and a bad text in a format string ends the text, instead of stopping the game.
Script array cycle guard: copying, comparing or dumping an array that holds itself stops where it meets itself, instead of running out of stack.
Script UI list sort by nested paths: SortUIListBox with a path through a child tile finds it on every item, so the list sorts; xNVSE finds it only on the first.

Script list and scan guard (the key keeps its old name): an inventory list or a form list the script commands walk that runs back into itself, GetPaired asking for the same stack again, or a cell scan (GetFirstRef, GetNumRefs, GetRefs and the rest) whose depth takes it past the cell grid's 8-bit positions ends the walk; a name xNVSE copies into a 256- or 512-byte buffer (GetAgeClass's race name, AddAnimation's and DelAnimation's name, the setting and file names GetNumericGameSetting, IsModLoaded and the rest take) is read whole when it is longer; the list SetHotkeyItem gives a stack gets the game's vtable; the token commands (GetTokenValue, SetTokenValue and the rest) answer for an item only in the base container (the Pip-Boy, for one); OutputLocalMapPicturesOverride draws the whole grid square; none of these stops or hangs the game.
